en: Obviously, it's part of Google search, so it's Google search signals everything from spam, what's content that could be spam?
zh: 显然，它是 Google 搜索的一部分，所以它是 Google 搜索信号，从垃圾邮件开始，什么内容可能是垃圾邮件？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we don't want to probably use in a response all the way to, wow, this is the most authoritative helpful piece of information.
zh: 我们可能不想在响应中使用它，一直到，哇，这是最具权威性、最有帮助的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to link to it and we're going to explain, hey, according to this website, check out that information and then you're going to go probably go see that yourself.
zh: 我们将链接到它，我们将解释，嘿，根据这个网站，查看那个信息，然后你可能会自己去看看。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's how we've thought about designing this.
zh: 这就是我们思考设计它的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've worked on a lot of AI products at this point, and it's not just Google or Artifact and Instagram, you did a lot of AI stuff.
zh: 此时你已经在很多 AI 产品上工作过了，不仅仅是 Google 或者 Artifact 和 Instagram，你做了很多 AI 的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's something you've learned about building AI products that you find maybe people don't truly understand, maybe something that's surprised you by building successful AI products?
zh: 关于构建 AI 产品你学到了什么，你发现人们可能并没有真正理解，或者通过构建成功的 AI 产品让你感到惊讶的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the most recent one, and this is true, something even within the last week or two, is that it's so obvious how human-like the interface is becoming with how you can communicate and steer AI.
zh: 我认为最近的一个，这是真的，甚至在过去一两周内，是关于你如何交流和引导 AI 的界面变得多么像人，这是显而易见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it used to be even just months back that you had to do a lot of work to get the AI to do the thing you're trying to get it to do, right?
zh: 我认为甚至在几个月前，你必须做很多工作才能让 AI 做你试图让它做的事情，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You had to do these incantations, you had to prompt in a really specific way.
zh: 你必须使用这些咒语，你必须以一种非常具体的方式进行提示。

speaker: Unknown
en: People would have all these hacks like, "Hey, act like you're a coach and you do these things," and you have to really push it, or to use a tool more on the technical side.
zh: 人们会有所有这些技巧，比如，“嘿，表现得像个教练，你做这些事情，”你必须真正推动它，或者更多地使用技术方面的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had to do post-training, you had to take this foundational model and you had to show it data, you had to train it and actually update its weights to do more sophisticated things.
zh: 你必须做后训练，你必须采用这个基础模型，你必须向它展示数据，你必须训练它并真正更新它的权重以做更复杂的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell it, "Hey, here's documentation for an API.
zh: 告诉它，“嘿，这是 API 的文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you ever have a problem, ping this API.
zh: 如果你遇到问题，调用这个 API。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's the data," as if it's an engineer that you had that you could talk to and it would have no idea what to do with that, or it would have some idea and wouldn't really do it.
zh: 这是数据，”就好像你有一个工程师，你可以和他交谈，但他不知道该做什么，或者他有一些想法但真的不会去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: But increasingly, you can just use language.
zh: 但越来越多地，你可以只使用语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost if you were to write up an order, you could be like, "Wow, I'm a new startup.
zh: 几乎就像如果你要写一个订单，你可能会说，「哇，我是个新创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's my data internally.
zh: 这是我内部的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here are the APIs to it.
zh: 这是它的 APIs。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's the schema and the URL.
zh: 这是架构和 URL。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's when to use it.
zh: 这是何时使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, make sure that if you get this kind of a question, you really make sure to get it right."
zh: 顺便说一下，确保如果你遇到这类问题，你一定要确保做对。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And that'll end up doing a lot in the model.
zh: 而这最终会在模型中产生很多效果。

speaker: Unknown
en: The model's been now encoded to be able to say, "Okay, I'm going to use more reasoning or thinking budget for that kind of a question."
zh: 模型现在已经编码能够说，「好的，对于这类问题，我将使用更多的推理或思考预算。」

speaker: Unknown
en: Or, "I'm going to use tools or code, use code execution in order to connect to this API I'm told about."
zh: 或者，「我将使用工具或代码，使用代码执行来连接到这个被告知的 API。」

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a relatively new thing.
zh: 这是一个相对新的事物。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think it's going to open up a lot of this democratization of accessing these models and building incredible things because you don't even need to do a lot.
zh: 所以我认为这将会开放很多获取这些模型和构建令人难以置信的事物的民主化，因为你甚至不需要做太多。

speaker: Unknown
en: To get the most sophisticated outcomes increasingly, I don't think you need to do a lot of this heavy duty fine-tuning.
zh: 为了获得最复杂的结果，越来越多地，我不认为你需要做很多这种繁重的微调。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes me think about, I had this recent guest, Nesrine Changuel, on the podcast.
zh: 这让我想到了，我最近有一位嘉宾，Nesrine Changuel，上了播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: She was a PM at Google, she worked on Google Meet, she was a delight PM working on at making products more delightful.
zh: 她是谷歌的产品经理，她在 Google Meet 上工作，她是一位致力于让产品更令人愉快的 delight PM。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she talked about the reason Google Meet did so well and is now feels like it's killing Zoom is they compared the experience of Google meet to a human meeting versus making it the best possible video conference, make this as good as a human experience.
zh: 她谈到了 Google Meet 做得这么好并且现在感觉像是正在扼杀 Zoom 的原因是，他们将 Google meet 的体验比作人类的会议，而不是把它做成最好的视频会议，使其像人类体验一样好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's interesting what you're talking about, how that's almost the goal here with AI is just make you feel like you're just talking to a person.
zh: 你所说的很有趣，这几乎就是 AI 的目标，就是让你觉得你只是在和一个人交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 正是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Might be obvious, but think about that.
zh: 这可能很明显，但想想看。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, let me zoom out and talk about, and let's talk about just broader lessons you've learned over the course of your career.
zh: 好的，让我缩一下，谈谈，让我们谈谈你在整个职业生涯中学到的更广泛的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've built a lot of very successful products, which I've shared in the intro at this point.
zh: 你构建了很多非常成功的产品，我在开场介绍中已经分享过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many also on the other side of the spectrum, we got the whole portfolio.
zh: 许多也在光谱的另一端，我们有了整个组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, perfect.
zh: 好的，完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll talk about some of that.
zh: 我们会谈谈其中的一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: I asked you as we were getting ready for this conversation, what's one thing you wanted to get across in this conversation?
zh: 当我们为这次谈话做准备时，我问过你，你想在这场对话中传达的一件事是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's something you think would be really helpful for product builders to hear to help them build more successful products?
zh: 你认为产品构建者听到什么会真正帮助他们构建更成功的产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you used this phrase: embodying relentless improvement.
zh: 你用了这个短语：体现无情的改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you just talk about that?
zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that mean?
zh: 这是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is this so important?
zh: 为什么这很重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, I mean, I think that you need to be the physical manifestation of two pieces of things.
zh: 当然，我认为你需要成为两件事物的物理化身。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is just relentlessness, just complete effort, but is always exerted in a direction of positive productivity.
zh: 一个只是无情，只是完全的努力，但总是朝着积极生产力的方向施力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the second is make things better.
zh: 然后第二个是把事情做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to always make things better, you're never content.
zh: 你必须总是把事情做得更好，你永远不会满足。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think this actually came out of a story, a little bit of a funny story where I was at Instagram at the time doing a big all team meeting, one of my first, and they had this icebreaker, what's one word to describe yourself?
zh: 我认为这实际上是出自一个故事，一个有点有趣的故事，当时我在 Instagram 参加一个大型的全体团队会议，我的第一次之一，他们有一个破冰环节，用一个词形容你自己？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in the backstage area, I texted my wife really quick.
zh: 所以在后台区域，我很快给我的妻子发了短信。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, "Hey, just one word to describe me, first thing that comes to your mind."
zh: 我说，「嘿，只用一个词形容我，你脑子里首先想到的东西。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And she just wrote back, "Dissatisfied."
zh: 她只是回复，「不满意的。」

speaker: Unknown
en: I was chuckling in the back room because I was first of all kind of offended because I was like, "It's not loving, caring, something good?"
zh: 我在后台咯咯笑，因为我首先有点被冒犯了，因为我想，「这不是充满爱、关怀，什么好的吗？」

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I saw her little bubble thing.
zh: 然后我看到了她的小气泡消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's like, "Okay, there's more."
zh: 她说，「好的，还有更多。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And then she wrote me this really thoughtful thing that was like, "It's not that you're just unhappy.
zh: 然后她给我写了这段非常感人的话，就像是，「并不是你不快乐。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like you want the world to be better.
zh: 而是你希望世界变得更美好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're driven out of a deep desire.
zh: 你是出于一种深沉的渴望被驱动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's that you feel this sense of dissatisfaction with what the world gives you.
zh: 是你对世界给你的东西感到一种不满意的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to make it better, and you're pushed and motivated to do that."
zh: 你想让它变得更好，并且你被推动和激励去这样做。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And I thought about that after.
zh: 之后我想到了那件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it wasn't until we built a bunch of products, some that didn't do well, some that have had a lot of really large success now, billions of people use them, where it felt like one of the big differences, obviously a lot of it is just the conditions of the product and a little bit of luck here and there too.
zh: 直到我们构建了一系列产品，有些做得不好，有些现在已经有了很大的成功，数十亿人在使用它们，感觉其中一个很大的区别，显然很多只是产品的条件以及这里和那里的一点运气。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for the things that went well, there was always this spirit of just we're going to get it eventually if we just make two more moves to make it better.
zh: 但对于那些进展顺利的事情，总是有一种精神，只要我们再做两步让它变得更好，我们最终就会得到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then eventually, as I talked about before earlier in our conversation, you get this tipping point where it just tips over into being net useful to people because of just that amount of compounding effort that you put into something because you're just always so... You're the harshest critic and the most dissatisfied person in the room about your own work basically.
zh: 然后最终，就像我们之前在谈话中谈到的那样，你会达到一个临界点，它只是倾覆为对人们有净用处，只是因为你投入在某种东西上的那种复利努力，因为你总是如此……基本上你是房间里对自己工作最严厉的批评者和最不满意的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's really meaningful.
zh: 我认为这非常有意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's this other incredible story that Tony Fadell told on a TED Talk 10 years ago.
zh: 还有另一个 Tony Fadell 10 年前在 TED 演讲中讲过的不可思议的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can look it up.
zh: 你们可以去查一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's something around Think Younger as a title.
zh: 我想标题大概是 Think Younger 之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he talks about what it means that as we grow up in age and become grownups, I have two little kids so that's something I think about a lot.
zh: 他讲的是随着我们长大并成为成年人意味着什么，我有两个小孩子，所以我经常思考这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We habituate to everything.
zh: 我们对所有事物都会产生适应。

speaker: Unknown
en: We accept and we tolerate what the world gives us everywhere, and we just go, "Oh, that kind of sucks.
zh: 我们在各处接受并忍受世界给我们的东西，我们只是说，「噢，那有点烂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, well," we shrug our shoulders and we move on.
zh: 噢，好吧」，我们耸耸肩然后继续前行。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you don't do that and you ask, "Why?
zh: 但如果你不那样做并且你问，「为什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: This sucks, why am I tolerating this and how do I make it better?"
zh: 这很烂，我为什么要忍受这个，以及我如何让它变得更好？」

speaker: Unknown
en: He has this incredible story about going grocery shopping, and he goes on for 10 minutes about this story almost it felt like where he talks about getting a piece of fruit like a plum or a peach, and how it has that sticker on it and it's got that sticker and who put that sticker there?
zh: 他有一个关于去杂货店购物的不可思议的故事，他花了差不多 10 分钟讲这个故事，感觉就像他在讲买一个像李子或桃子这样的水果，它上面有那个贴纸，它有那个贴纸，是谁把那个贴纸贴在那里的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then when you get home, you take your fruit out of your bag, you're ready to eat it, you're all excited, you stick your thumb under the sticker, it punctures the flesh.
zh: 然后当你回到家，你把水果从袋子里拿出来，你准备吃它，你很兴奋，你把大拇指伸到贴纸下面，它刺破了果肉。

speaker: Unknown
en: He goes into just incredible detail about how it punctures the flesh of the fruit.
zh: 他极其详细地描述了它是如何刺破水果果肉的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The sticker comes off now, the fruit's bleeding, then you flick the sticker.
zh: 贴纸现在掉了下来，水果在流血（汁液），然后你弹那个贴纸。

speaker: Unknown
en: The sticker misses the garbage, you bend over and pick it up, you put the sticker back in.
zh: 贴纸没扔进垃圾桶，你弯腰捡起它，你把贴纸放回去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, "Wow, that is embodying this mentality of just why is this here?
zh: 然后我想，「哇，这就是体现了那种心态，就是为什么这东西在这里？

speaker: Unknown
en: How can this be better?"
zh: 这怎么能变得更好？」

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the best product people, the best thinkers in the space, that's how they think, in my opinion.
zh: 我认为最好的产品人员，这个领域最优秀的思想家，在我看来就是这样思考的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine there are many examples of you doing this in the many products you worked on.
zh: 我想象在你工作的许多产品中都有很多你这样做的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there one that comes to mind as a good example of this inaction of this actually working really well and delivering something really huge?
zh: 有没有想到一个例子能很好地说明这种不作为实际上非常有效并交付了非常重要的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, honestly, a big thing is working on AI Mode.
zh: 坦率地说，一件大事就是致力于 AI Mode。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of it was we saw in AI Overviews that people were trying to ask harder questions and we weren't able to answer a bunch of them, or AI Overviews just didn't show up.
zh: 我认为很大程度上是因为我们在 AI Overviews 中看到人们试图问更难的问题，而我们无法回答其中许多问题，或者 AI Overviews 根本没有出现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a bunch of us sat around and we're like, "Why can't you just do this for everything?"
zh: 所以我们一群人坐在一起想，「为什么你不能直接为所有事情做这个？」

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead of saying, "Oh, we don't need to solve for that," or, "That's not something that's in the most addressable next thing."
zh: 而不是说，「噢，我们不需要为此解决这个问题」，或者，「那不是下一个最可解决的事情里的一项。」

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like we actually saw people in the query stream putting the words AI at the end of their queries because they're trying to get the AI to do the thing.
zh: 实际上是因为我们看到人们在查询流中把 AI 这个词加在他们的查询末尾，因为他们试图让 AI 做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would look at that and be like, "This is ridiculous.
zh: 我们看到那个然后想，「这太荒谬了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to build something here."
zh: 我们需要在这里构建一些东西。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was one of the big motivations, was actually identifying that user problem, being very disgruntled on behalf of the user.
zh: 那是主要的动力之一，实际上是识别出了那个用户问题，代表用户感到非常不满。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just failing the user every day.
zh: 我们每天都在辜负用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are not helping them actually get their thing better understood, and we're going to go build a whole thing because of it, because that's hard to do by the way, to build all of that.
zh: 我们没有帮助他们真正更好地理解他们的事情，我们要为此去构建一个完整的东西，顺便说一句，这很难做到，要构建所有那些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it just was so obvious that that's what we needed to do.
zh: 但显然那就是我们需要做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's two buckets of people.
zh: 有两类人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say hypothetically, one bucket is just make things better, make amazing experiences, you're going to do great.
zh: 假设有一类人只是让事物变得更好，创造惊人的体验，你会做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's another bucket that's like drive metrics, drive goals, hit our KPIs.
zh: 还有一类人像是驱动指标，驱动目标，达成我们的 KPI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know what you're not saying is just work on things, just make things better, relentlessly, make things better.
zh: 我知道你（本来）没有说的是只致力于这些事，只是让事情变得更好，不懈地，让事情变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you just think about, I guess that overlap of okay, makes things better, but also here's what we really, here's the strategy, here's the vision.
zh: 你怎么想，我猜想那个重叠的部分，好吧，让事情变得更好，但这也是真正的策略，这是愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think?
zh: 你怎么思考？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I don't think of them as an or.
zh: 是的，我不认为它们是二选一的（或）关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they have to be intersected because basically the way I think about it is you actually start with a problem or the inverse of that, which is a vision, but they're connected.
zh: 我认为它们必须相交，因为基本上我思考的方式是你实际上从一个问题开始，或者它的反面，也就是愿景，但它们是相连的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most great companies, most great products come out of a problem, but out of the problem becomes like, "Here's a better way."
zh: 大多数伟大的公司，大多数伟大的产品都出自一个问题，但从问题中变成了，「这里有更好的方法。」

speaker: Unknown
en: What if instead of this crappy thing or way of living or thing that we all tolerate and accept, some entrepreneur comes up and says, "What if we did this other thing?"
zh: 如果不做这个烂东西、这种生活方式或我们都容忍和接受的这件事，某个企业家出来说，「如果我们做另一件事会怎样？」

speaker: Unknown
en: So it comes out of this dissatisfaction and this sense of better that you need to make things better, but then you're going to build, and at the end of the day, you need your instrumentation to know if you're on the right track.
zh: 所以它出自这种不满和这种更好的感觉，你需要让事情变得更好，但然后你要构建，在一天结束时，你需要你的仪表化（instrumentation）工具来知道你是否在正确的轨道上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where you bring tools like, okay, you build your first version of the product, do people like it?
zh: 那就是你要引入工具的地方，好吧，你构建产品的第一个版本，人们喜欢它吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then each product goes through its journey.
zh: 然后每个产品都会经历它的旅程。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way understand that people like it is you scrutinize.
zh: 了解人们喜欢它的方式是你进行详细审查。

speaker: Unknown
en: Typically, you talk to people, but you also add some analytical tools there.
zh: 通常，你和人交谈，但你也会在那里添加一些分析工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might look at something like a J-curve.
zh: 你可能会看像 J 曲线这样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the retention, the percentage of people still using the product day seven, day 30, day 90, and does it flatten or do people just drip out of there?
zh: 这是留存率，第 7 天、第 30 天、第 90 天仍在使用产品的人的百分比，它会趋于平稳还是人们只是从那里流失？

speaker: Unknown
en: Over time, it's just not exciting people.
zh: 随着时间的推移，它只是不再让人们兴奋了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that would go to zero if on a long enough timeline, no one's going to use it.
zh: 如果时间线足够长，它会归零，没有人会使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't get past that, you toast right then.
zh: 你如果不能度过那个阶段，你就直接完蛋了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, some people are doing it, okay, great.
zh: 好的，有些人在做这件事，好的，很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need more people to do it, and it needs to be good enough that people talk about it and then it grows.
zh: 我们需要更多的人去做这件事，而且它需要足够好，以至于人们谈论它然后它就会增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's another gate.
zh: 所以这是另一道门槛。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's another one which is, well, how big can this get actually, is it a small thing?
zh: 然后还有另一个问题，就是这个东西实际上能做多大，它是个小东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it a medium thing?
zh: 它是个中等的东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think most companies, you have an aspiration of being big, but you can't start big.
zh: 我认为大多数公司，你有变大的愿望，但你不能从大开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone's got to go through that journey.
zh: 每个人都要经历那段旅程。

speaker: Unknown
en: No product has started big.
zh: 没有产品是从大开始的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even ones that get big really quickly, even a week quickly, they had something.
zh: 即使那些真的很快变大的产品，即使是快到一周，它们也有一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then even internally, they started small.
zh: 然后即使在内部，它们也是从小开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: They started small with a hundred to 100 people, and so you have to be metrics focused, I think in order to know if you're doing the right thing.
zh: 它们从小开始，拥有 100 到 100 人，所以你必须关注指标，我认为为了知道你在做正确的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the other thing is, on the other side of the spectrum, you're running a big thing, and there, you need metrics to be your guide.
zh: 然后另一件事是，在频谱的另一端，你在运行一个大东西，在那里你需要指标成为你的向导。

speaker: Unknown
en: If your product, let's say, let's say our core metrics down 5% this week, it's like, well, what's going on?
zh: 如果你的产品，比如说，假设我们的核心指标本周下降了 5%，这就像是，嗯，发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you be really close to root cause analysis there and say, "Well, actually it turns out that it's an issue.
zh: 所以你在那里非常接近根本原因分析并说，“嗯，实际上结果发现这是一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it in a region?
zh: 它是在一个区域吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it on a device?
zh: 它是在一个设备上吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it in a demographic?
zh: 它是在一个人口统计中吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it in a use case?
zh: 它是在一个用例中吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where does my problem lie?"
zh: 我的问题出在哪里？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then when you get to it, you understand the problem and then this improvement thing comes back where it's like, "Okay, I'm going to fix that thing.
zh: 然后当你开始着手时，你理解了这个问题，然后这个改进的事情回来了，就像是，“好的，我要修复那个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the treatment for that disease?"
zh: 针对那个疾病的治疗方法是什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you're back to growth again, and so you need this and you always are looking at what's the system that I'm working on and what are my instruments?
zh: 然后你又回到了增长，所以你需要这个并且你总是看着我正在工作的系统是什么以及我的仪器是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a pilot to know if this thing is going and flying correctly, but then it doesn't tell you exactly what to do, you have to thank for yourself how to make it better.
zh: 我是一名飞行员，要知道这个东西是否正在正确地飞行，但是它没有确切地告诉你该做什么，你必须为了自己去思考如何让它变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can just show you a little bit of the way.
zh: 我只能给你指一小段路。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that you just gave a master class on just how to prioritize and pick what to work on.
zh: 我喜欢你刚才给出了一个大师课，关于如何优先处理和选择要做什么工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to go on a quick tangent.
zh: 我想快速跑个题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of products that have done really well and become really big, Stories, you build and launched Stories at Instagram.
zh: 说到那些做得很好并且变得很大的产品，Stories（快拍），你在 Instagram 构建并发布了 Stories。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's quite an infamous product launch back in the day, it was quite controversial because it basically took what Snapchat was doing really well and then, "Hey, let's bring it to Instagram," and it was not great for Snapchat.
zh: 当时这是一个非常臭名昭著的产品发布，因为它非常有争议，因为它基本上拿了 Snapchat 做得很好的东西，然后，“嘿，让我们把它带到 Instagram”，这对 Snapchat 来说并不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now that it was so long ago and just, it's so far in the past, I'm so curious just to hear about that time reflecting on just that decision, what you guys talked about, how you decided to go ahead with that and anything just, I don't know, you think about looking back at that.
zh: 既然那是很久以前的事了，只是，它太遥远了在过去，我很好奇只是听听那段时光反思那个决定，你们谈论了什么，你们如何决定继续进行以及任何只是，我不知道，你认为回头看那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a couple of really important lessons from that launch.
zh: 我认为那次发布有几个非常重要的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I mean we went on afterwards to launch Reels, a bunch of updates to direct messaging, we had feed rank game.
zh: 我的意思是我们后来继续发布了 Reels，对直接消息的一堆更新，我们有 feed rank game。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was just a huge era there when I was there between 2016 and 2021 or so where just so many new products got built.
zh: 在我在那里的 2016 年到 2021 年左右之间有一段巨大的时期，那时许多新产品被构建出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think an interesting lesson in all of those, and particularly in Stories was you have to really understand why someone uses your product and know when something is actually an existential question because there's just a better format or a different way of doing something that has worked and works and you need to figure out what that might mean for you, because not every great thing is going to be invented by you.
zh: 我认为所有这些中的一个有趣的教训，特别是在 Stories 中，你必须真正理解为什么有人使用你的产品并知道什么时候这实际上是一个存在问题，因为有只是更好的格式或不同的做事方式已经奏效并且有效你需要弄清楚那对你意味着什么，因为不是每一件伟大的事情都会由你发明。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that a lot of these things are, they can become formats that you can make your own and you need to learn from the world and what's happening out there in order for your product to always give the best thing to its users.
zh: 但我认为这些事情中的很多是，它们可以成为你自己的格式，你需要从世界和外面正在发生的事情中学习，以便你的产品总是给它的用户最好的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for Stories, we looked at Instagram like, what's the point of Instagram?
zh: 所以对于 Stories，我们看着像这样的 Instagram，Instagram 的意义是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It is sharing your life and connecting with people ultimately.
zh: 它最终是分享你的生活和与人联系。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if there's a way to do that, that lowers the pressure because it doesn't have likes or it's just ephemeral format and it's optimized well for mobile because it's this full screen experience.
zh: 如果有一种方法可以做到这一点，降低压力因为它没有点赞或者它只是一个短暂的格式并且它为移动端做了很好的优化，因为它是这种全屏体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a really great format and kudos to Snapchat for inventing it.
zh: 它真的是一个非常棒的格式，赞扬 Snapchat 发明了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't think of that as a deterrent, that we had to go make Instagram photo clock.
zh: 我们不认为那是一个阻碍，我们必须去制作 Instagram photo clock。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, there were early versions of this idea where you try to take the core Instagram feed and make it ephemeral.
zh: 实际上，这个想法有早期版本，你试图拿核心的 Instagram feed 并把它变成短暂的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And whenever you try to mix a core product that's very cemented in someone's mind and physically looks a specific way and you're trying to make, contort it to do something new, it's usually a bad recipe.
zh: 每当你试图混合一个核心产品，它在某人的脑海中非常根深蒂固并且物理上看是一种特定的方式，你正在试图使，扭曲它去做一些新事情，这通常是一个坏的配方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we knew we needed to do something new and then it was so clearly was critical to the core essence of what the product could do, could fit in naturally.
zh: 所以我们知道我们需要做一些新的事情，然后它是如此清楚地是产品核心功能的关键，可以自然地适应。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the question was how do we make it our own?
zh: 但问题是我们如何使它成为我们自己的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do we build on this?
zh: 我们如何在此基础上构建？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you think, there were a bunch of things that we did that made it Instagram.
zh: 所以如果你想一想，我们做了一些事情使它成为 Instagram。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, it had different creative tools and it had things like neon drawing and these really sophisticated filters that people loved.
zh: 例如，它有不同的创意工具，它有像霓虹绘图这样的东西，还有这些人们真的非常喜欢的复杂滤镜。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also looked at this talk about being dissatisfied.
zh: 我们也看了这个关于不满足的谈话。

speaker: Unknown
en: People took, a lot of times they want their main camera to take a picture of something and then they want to upload it to Instagram because they want to save it and they want it to be in a very high quality, high resolution photo, because it's a memory.
zh: 人们拍，很多时候他们想要他们的主相机拍某样东西的照片，然后他们想把它上传到 Instagram，因为他们想保存它，他们希望它是一张非常高质量、高分辨率的照片，因为它是一个记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Snapchat at the time didn't allow you to upload photos, it was like you have to use the Snap camera.
zh: Snapchat 当时不允许你上传照片，它就像是你必须使用 Snap 相机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we made a bunch of decisions like that where why don't you just let people upload their photo?
zh: 所以我们做了一堆那样的决定，比如为什么不干脆让人们上传他们的照片？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is back to the dissatisfied point, that's frustrating.
zh: 这又回到了那个不满意的点，这很令人沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or there's another example where you couldn't pause if you were consuming a story.
zh: 或者有另一个例子，如果你在消费一个故事，你无法暂停。

speaker: Unknown
en: You couldn't pause it, it just would go through and be done because it was this ephemeral thing and you wanted to create safety.
zh: 你无法暂停它，它只会一直播放直到结束，因为这是一个稍纵即逝的东西，而且你想创造安全性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why can't you just pause?
zh: 为什么你不能直接暂停？

speaker: Unknown
en: It goes by too fast.
zh: 它过得太快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we added this pause, it's such a small thing, but you put your finger down to pause the story now.
zh: 所以我们添加了这个暂停功能，这是一个非常小的功能，但现在你把手指按下来就可以暂停故事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there were a whole set of those things that were shipped that made Stories feel Instagram.
zh: 因此有一整套这样的东西被发布出来，让 Stories 感觉像 Instagram。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't like you just had some other thing.
zh: 并不是说你只是有了一些其他东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it turns out that worked incredibly well, and so much to the fact that someone on the team mentioned that they always felt like at the time, they didn't realize it, but it was almost like it was missing the story size holes at the top of the page and it completed the product in some weird way for them.
zh: 结果证明效果非常好，以至于团队里有一个人提到，他们总是觉得当时并没有意识到这一点，但这几乎就像页面顶部缺少了那些故事大小的圆孔，以某种奇怪的方式为他们完成了这个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that was, I think an important lesson.
zh: 所以我认为这是一个重要的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instagram definitely got a lot of hate for that moment from a lot of founders.
zh: Instagram 当时确实从很多创始人那里招致了很多仇恨。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was just like, "Hey, you guys just stole this idea and that sucks."
zh: 就像是，“嘿，你们 guys 只是偷了这个主意，这很糟糕。”

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you guys just deal with that internally?
zh: 你们内部是如何处理这个的？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was just this is, "We got to do this.
zh: 就是这个，“我们必须做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got to focus on our shareholders and grow this thing," and that's how it goes sometimes?
zh: 我们必须专注于我们的股东并发展这个东西，”有时就是这样吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think it's more that we're focused on our users and the people who are loving Instagram and it's denying them the opportunity to have an easy way to just share a photo and have the thing go away.
zh: 我的意思是，我认为更多是我们专注于我们的用户和那些热爱 Instagram 的人，如果剥夺他们机会去拥有一种简单的方式来分享照片并让照片消失，那就是在否认他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, that's ultimately what we were trying to add.
zh: 我的意思是，这就是我们最终试图添加的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the end of the day, that is a format that people adopt.
zh: 归根结底，这是一种人们采用的形式。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the same way that you think about feeds, I think we talked about this at the time too when we shipped it.
zh: 就像你考虑信息流一样，我想我们当时发布它时也谈到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Facebook probably created the modern feed, but there's a feed for every single product.
zh: Facebook 可能创造了现代的信息流，但每个单一产品都有一个信息流。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a LinkedIn feed and there's a feed for DoorDash.
zh: 有一个 LinkedIn 信息流，也有一个 DoorDash 信息流。

speaker: Unknown
en: These things become core primitives quickly and formats, and then at the end of the day, you're just robbing your user base of the opportunity to have a better product if you're not making the best possible product for your use cases.
zh: 这些东西很快就成为了核心原语和形式，然后归根结底，如果你没有为你的用例制造最好的产品，你就是在剥夺你的用户群拥有更好产品的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for Instagram, it's used differently.
zh: 对于 Instagram 来说，它的使用方式不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: People use Instagram differently than they use other products.
zh: 人们使用 Instagram 的方式与他们使用其他产品的方式不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns out that there were these experiences in WhatsApp and in Messenger and in many other social products over time, and they all were used differently actually, which is fascinating.
zh: 事实证明，在 WhatsApp、Messenger 和许多其他社交产品中都有这些体验，而且它们实际上使用方式都不同，这很迷人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something else I want to talk about is you came into two products that were already doing really well, Instagram and Google.
zh: 我想谈论的另一件事是，你进入了两个已经运行良好的产品，Instagram 和 Google。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on the Instagram side, a transformative growth and improvement.
zh: 在 Instagram 方面，是转型式的增长和改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: Google is happening, we're in the middle of the improvement and growth you're driving.
zh: Google 正在发生，我们正处于你推动的改进和增长的中间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not a lot of people get to do this where they go into an existing product, make it grow significantly.
zh: 没有多少人能这样做，他们进入一个现有产品，使其显著增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people want to do this.
zh: 很多人想这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have a product that's been around for a long time.
zh: 他们有一个已经存在很久的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, how do we make this grow and be more successful?
zh: 嘿，我们如何让这个增长并更成功？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything specifically that you've learned about just coming into an existing product, figuring out where the big opportunities are and then just hockey-sticking growth?
zh: 关于进入一个现有产品，找出大机会在哪里，然后让增长呈现曲棍球棒式增长，你有什么具体学到的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because this is what everyone wants to do.
zh: 因为这是每个人都想做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a couple lessons here.
zh: 这里有几个教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think, by the way, the first lesson is to be humble always because it's extremely incredible to be able to work on products that have such impact on people.
zh: 我想顺便说一句，第一个教训是永远要谦虚，因为能够对人们有如此重大影响的产品工作是极其不可思议的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I view product like golf, you're always one stroke away from shanking.
zh: 我把产品看作高尔夫，你总是离打歪一杆之遥。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as soon as you think you're good, you're not, you don't know anything.
zh: 一旦你认为你很棒，你就不是了，你什么都不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: The world changes quickly.
zh: 世界变化很快。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to always be a servant to your user base and the people that are out there and learn from them.
zh: 你必须永远是你用户群和外面那些人的仆人，并向他们学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first thing I always do and think about is you get in touch in terms of why are people using this product, and where are the areas of growth?
zh: 我总是做的和想到的第一件事就是，就人们为什么使用这个产品以及增长领域在哪里而言，你要与之建立联系。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so usually even in a big product or a mature in a complex system, there's a part of it that's growing.
zh: 所以通常即使在一个大产品或一个成熟在一个复杂的系统中，也有一部分在增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a part of it that's mature, there could be a part of it that's declining or isn't growing as much.
zh: 有一部分是成熟的，可能有一部分在衰退或没有那么多增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Certainly in Instagram, there's been a big shift over the years of sharing into public very large broadcast posts and feed into these more lightweight formats like Stories and DM actually private sharing as well.
zh: 当然在 Instagram 中，多年来分享到非常大的公开广播帖子和信息流到这些更轻量级的形式如 Stories 和 DM 实际上私人分享也有很大的转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you have to observe that because every month, every year, the world changes, people's needs change.
zh: 所以你必须观察这一点，因为每个月，每年，世界都在变，人们的需求在变。

speaker: Unknown
en: First thing you do is you get a sense of what do people want out of this product?
zh: 你做的第一件事是你了解人们想从这个产品中得到什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's its true essence?
zh: 它的真正本质是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot about this job to be done framework, which is one of the things that I'm a big fan of and Clayton Christensen's book on Competing Against Luck is one of my favorite books on this topic where you have to really be a student of causation.
zh: 我对这个待完成任务框架考虑很多，这是我很喜欢的东西之一，Clayton Christensen 的《与运气竞争》一书是我关于这个主题的最喜欢的书之一，在这个主题上你必须真正成为因果关系的学生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is someone using this product?
zh: 为什么有人使用这个产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are they doing with it and what are they trying to get done with it?
zh: 他们在用它做什么，他们试图用它完成什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that usually leads you to do bigger next stage ideas, and it removes this belief that you need to solve the problem with the current tools.
zh: 这通常会引导你去做更大的下一阶段想法，并且它消除了这种信念，即你需要用现有工具来解决问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the Instagram version, it was like you have to make a square photo do more for people.
zh: 在 Instagram 版本中，就像是你必须让方形照片为人们做更多事。

speaker: Unknown
en: That would be how you increment the product.
zh: 那就是你 increment 产品的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or in Google's example, there's something very specific with the core search experience that needs to change, it's a subtle tweak.
zh: 或者在 Google 的例子中，核心搜索体验有一些非常具体的东西需要改变，这是一个微妙的调整。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to think, well, what's the big thing?
zh: 你必须思考，好吧，大东西是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone's trying to ask a really hard question out of Google?
zh: 有人正试图向 Google 提出一个非常难的问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the best way to do that for them?
zh: 为他们做到这一点的最佳方式是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it makes you think more first principled and that's the first basis of this.
zh: 所以它让你更多地思考第一性原理，这是这第一基础。

en: And so what's interesting is then you think, well, how do I bring that into my world?
zh: 所以有趣的是，你会想，好吧，我如何把它带入我的世界？

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: People have a set of expectations you need to snap to for those use cases.

en: And then you are constantly learning how to best make these new products work within your world.
zh: 然后你不断学习如何最好地让这些新产品在你的世界里工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You never just want to snap in something that's working, you have to make it work for your users, your expectations, and what people are trying to do with your product.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 还是我们只是在自我祝贺？

en: Ultimately you want to have impact on people and that's what matters.
zh: 最终你希望对人们产生影响，这才是最重要的。

zh: Google 在大约一年的时间里从一个想法到搜索体验的一个重大改变，这是一个 AI 驱动的，这令人难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is not what people imagine Google is like, and it feels like things are different and things have changed in how you guys operate.

en: Is it just top-down leadership, we need to get shit done, or is there something more?
zh: 只是自上而下的领导力吗，我们需要把事情搞定，还是有更多的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I mean I think it's interesting how organizations change.
zh: 不，我认为组织如何变化是很有趣的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think when you feel like there is a moment in time that is clearly critical to deliver for people, people are trying to get information from Google.
zh: 我认为当你觉得有一个时刻显然是至关重要的，要为人们交付，人们正试图从 Google 获取信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are not able to answer certain things or help people in certain ways and there's this technology that can do it, that creates urgency, and obviously there's lots of people building lots of things and the market's crazy and there's lots of things shipping all the time.
zh: 我们无法回答某些事情或以某种方式帮助人们，而这种技术可以做到，这就产生了紧迫感，显然有很多人在构建很多东西，市场很疯狂，一直有东西在发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a really exciting and healthy moment for us to build and build quickly and I think it's just exciting to be able to capture that opportunity because I think people believe, and I certainly believe that the next year or so of product is going to establish how people use the next wave of products for many years.
zh: 对我们来说，这是一个非常令人兴奋和健康的时刻去构建并快速构建，我认为能够抓住这个机会只是令人兴奋，因为我认为人们相信，当然我也相信，大约一年的产品将确立人们如何使用下一波产品好多年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so at least I can only speak for myself, I feel this obligation to our users to give them the best version of Google that's powered by AI and that gives them the full knowledge of everything Google knows about the world and information to people and accessible with AI.
zh: 所以至少我只能代表我自己，我感到对我们的用户有一种义务，给他们最好的 Google 版本，它是 AI 驱动的，并将 Google 所知道的关于世界的一切的全部知识以及信息带给人们，并通过 AI 访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's driving a lot of the excitement.
zh: 这正在驱动很多兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's such a good point that people are building their new habits.
zh: 是的，这是一个很好的观点，人们正在建立他们的新习惯。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's wild how many people just now rely on ChatGPT and how quickly that happened.
zh: 现在有多少人只是依赖 ChatGPT，以及这种情况发生得有多快，这太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I could see Google being worried that, oh, shit, everyone's changing their habit from searching Google to searching ChatGPT.
zh: 我能看到 Google 担心，哦，该死，每个人都在把他们的习惯从搜索 Google 改变成搜索 ChatGPT。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the fact that now Gemini is number one.
zh: 而且事实上现在 Gemini 是第一名。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was actually looking at the list of top, so in the top 15 apps, Google is I think five of them, a third.
zh: 我实际上在看顶级应用的列表，所以在前 15 名应用中，Google 占了其中 5 个，三分之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's out of control, killing it.
zh: 这有点失控，做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: When people look at AI Mode versus ChatGPT or Claude or let's even say Perplexity, what's the way you think about the positioning of AI Mode versus these other tools?
zh: 当人们看 AI Mode 与 ChatGPT 或 Claude，或者我们甚至可以说 Perplexity 相比时，你如何思考 AI Mode 相对于这些其他工具的定位？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it trying to be a direct competitor or is it just like, "No, it's actually pretty different and here's what it's for?"
zh: 它是试图成为一个直接的竞争对手，还是就像这样，“不，它实际上相当不同，这就是它的用途？”

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean AI Mode's a way to ask search anything you want.
zh: 是的，我的意思是 AI Mode 是一种向搜索询问任何你想问的问题的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's designed and specially created for information.
zh: 它是为信息专门设计和创造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so really, it should give incredible helpful responses for the things that people come to Google for.
zh: 所以真的，它应该为人们来 Google 寻找的东西提供令人难以置信的有用的回应。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about you're planning a trip, you're trying to buy something, you're working through a question for your research project.
zh: 想想你在计划一次旅行，你试图购买某样东西，你正在为你的研究项目解决一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It needs information and that's really, it's less focused on things like creativity, although there's things that can do that are nice there.
zh: 它需要信息，这实际上，它较少关注像创造力这样的事情，虽然有一些事情可以做到那也不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can help you.
zh: 它可以帮助你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just like any kind of core AI product, you can ask it to rewrite something for you, it'll do that.
zh: 就像任何一种核心 AI 产品一样，你可以要求它为你重写一些东西，它会做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we are less focused on creativity, productivity, upload a spreadsheet and output graphs for me, we're not focused on that.
zh: 但我们较少关注创造力、生产力、上传一个电子表格并为我输出图表，我们不关注那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're really focused on what people use Google for, and making an AI for that so that you can come to Google, ask whatever you want and get effortless information about that and context and links to then also verify, dig in and go to the authoritative sources ultimately that people want, and we hear from people.
zh: 我们真的关注人们使用 Google 做什么，并为此做一个 AI，这样你可以来到 Google，问任何你想问的，并获得关于它的轻松的信息，以及上下文和链接，然后也可以验证，深入研究并最终去到人们想要的权威来源，我们从人们那里听到。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those ends up becoming the distinct qualities of this product versus more of a chatbot.
zh: 所以这些最终成为这个产品相对于更多聊天机器人的独特品质。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you would talk to it like you maybe even have a bit of a, "Hey, how are you doing today," with that chatbot that we have some of that, we see that a little bit, but people are usually coming for information.
zh: 也许你会像跟它说话，甚至可能有点像，“嘿，你今天怎么样，”和那个聊天机器人，我们有一些那个，我们看到了一点，但人们通常是来寻找信息的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're trying to learn something and we focused our product on that.
zh: 他们试图学习一些东西，我们的产品专注于那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Got it.
zh: 明白了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, AI Mode is not your therapist.
zh: 好的，AI Mode 不是你的治疗师。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe zooming out again a little bit and reflecting on all the amazing products you've worked on, all the places you've worked, if you had to pick two or three just core product principles or philosophies that have helped you build such amazing and successful products, what would those be?
zh: 也许再次稍微拉远视角，反思你工作过的所有令人惊叹的产品，你工作过的所有地方，如果你必须挑选两三个核心产品原则或哲学，它们帮助你构建了如此令人惊叹和成功的产品，那些会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What comes to mind?
zh: 你想到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, there's typically three things I think about.
zh: 我的意思是，通常我考虑三件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I were to write a book about how to build great products, there'd be three chapters.
zh: 如果我要写一本关于如何构建伟大产品的书，会有三章。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean there'd probably more than that, but three chapters.
zh: 我的意思是可能不止那个，但三章。

speaker: Lenny
en: I love that. I love how short that would be. That's the ideal book.
zh: 我喜欢那个。我喜欢那个会有多短。那是理想的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've thought about these three areas now for a while and it's like they're always consistently the three things.
zh: 我已经思考这三个领域一段时间了，而且它们一直始终是这三件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is deeply understand people, and I think we talked about this a little bit with the jobs to be done point and Clayton Christensen's book, which I loved around Competing Against Luck.
zh: 第一个是深刻理解人，我认为我们用待完成任务的观点和 Clayton Christensen 的书稍微聊过这个，我很喜欢《与运气竞争》。

speaker: Unknown
en: It really helps you be a student of why someone ends up, in his words, hiring a product.
zh: 它真的帮助你成为学生，研究为什么会有人，用他的话来说，雇佣一个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't think of users as using your product.
zh: 不要把用户想成是在使用你的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think of users as hiring you to do something for them.
zh: 把用户想成是雇佣你为他们做某事。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this famous quote, I think it's Theodore Levitt had, "People don't want a quarter inch drill, they want a quarter inch hole."
zh: 有这句名言，我想是 Theodore Levitt 说的，“人们不想要一个四分之一英寸的钻头，他们想要一个四分之一英寸的孔。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So what is someone trying to do?
zh: 所以某人是在试图做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to understand that deeply and then you can build an amazing product.
zh: 你必须深刻理解那个，然后你就能构建一个惊人的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also by the way, when you go back, why someone not using your product?
zh: 而且还有顺便说一句，当你回过头，为什么有人不用你的产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it focuses on these techniques to extract causation.
zh: 所以它专注于这些技术来提取因果关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he actually talks a lot about this interview.
zh: 所以他实际上谈了很多关于这个面试。

speaker: Unknown
en: He calls it an interrogation where you talk to a user like, "Hey, why do you use my product?
zh: 他称之为审讯，在那里你跟一个用户交谈，“嘿，你为什么用我的产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where were you?
zh: 你在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: Were you in bed?
zh: 你在床上吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Were you at work?
zh: 你在工作吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What were you doing?"
zh: 你在做什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: "Oh, I was talking to my wife in the morning."
zh: “噢，我在早上跟我妻子谈话。”

speaker: Unknown
en: "Okay, well, what brought it up?"
zh: “好的，是什么把它带出来的？”

speaker: Unknown
en: "Well, I guess I was reading the newspaper."
zh: “嗯，我想我在看报纸。”

speaker: Unknown
en: "Okay, well why?"
zh: “好的，为什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you have this aha moment like that when they first decide to use your product, he calls it the big hire.
zh: 然后你有这个顿悟时刻，像当他们第一次决定使用你的产品时，他称之为大雇佣。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is information that you obtain ends up becoming the most critical because that is what caused someone to use your product.
zh: 那是你获得的信息结果变成了最关键的，因为那是导致某人使用你产品的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you can study that and understand it, you'll be much more on your way than just building things that sound cool.
zh: 如果你能研究那个并理解它，你会比仅仅构建听起来很酷的东西更有进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's the first chapter is deeply understand people.
zh: 所以第一章是深刻理解人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second is really around analytical rigor and understanding your problems.
zh: 第二个真的围绕分析严谨性和理解你的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to understand your problems.
zh: 你必须理解你的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this got is a little bit of what we were talking about about root cause analysis and understanding, okay, the metrics are dropping.
zh: 这稍微一点是我们关于根因分析和理解的谈话，好的，指标在下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why?
zh: 为什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: If someone's not using your product, why?
zh: 如果有人不用你的产品，为什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And really being able to dissect that to get to true root causes.
zh: 并且真的能够解剖那个来到达真正的根本原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, well, they went all the way to the end and then bailed, and then you understand what turns out that it was most, we actually learned about this and there's a story in Close Friends at Instagram where it just totally failed at first in a bunch just when we shipped it.
zh: 就像，嗯，他们一路走到尽头然后退出了，然后你理解结果那是大多数，我们实际上学到了这个并且在 Instagram 的 Close Friends 有个故事，那里它一开始就完全失败了，就在我们发布它的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turned out that we looked at the data and people were only adding one close friend to their list because it was mistranslated as best friend in many markets.
zh: 结果是我们看了数据并且人们只加了一个亲密好友到他们的列表，因为在许多市场它被误翻译成了最好的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: So people just put one person and then the probability that person saw it and wrote back to you was zero.
zh: 所以人们只放了一个人然后那个人看到并回信给你的概率是零。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a product which is broken.
zh: 这是一个损坏的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like you got to understand your problems.
zh: 所以就像你必须理解你的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the third one's around really designing for clarity instead of cleverness.
zh: 第三个围绕真的为清晰度而不是聪明设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people are like, "Oh, we're going to differentiate the design," and we talked about this a little bit with Stories.
zh: 很多人像，“噢，我们要让设计差异化”，我们用 Stories 稍微聊过这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to make a new version of something, but if something's a standard and people understand it, if you lean into it, you're going to get so much leverage than if you reinvent it, and you have to be really thoughtful around when you reinvent and where you don't.
zh: 我们要制作某物的新版本，但如果某物是标准的并且人们理解它，如果你利用它，你会比重新发明它获得多得多的杠杆，你必须真的很深思熟虑关于你何时重新发明以及何时不。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think on this one, there's this great, Don Norman's book.
zh: 我认为在这个上面，有这本很棒的，Don Norman 的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, Design of Everyday Things is a big one, but he has this incredible chapter in there about doors, and why is it that after all of these years you walk up to a door, and based on how they're designed at times, people still don't know if you should pull or push that door because if you try to build the as beautiful symmetric two handles on each side on a glass door, it doesn't communicate in for any information to you.
zh: 显然，《设计心理学》是个大书，但他在那里有这不可思议的一章关于门，为什么是那样经过所有这些年你走到一扇门前，并且基于有时它们怎么设计的，人们仍然不知道你应该拉还是推那扇门，因为如果你试着建造一个漂亮的对称两边两个把手在玻璃门上，它没有传达任何信息给你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's lots of, I've seen all the time we've designed new icons when we could have used global icons like, "Oh, wouldn't it be so cool if we used a camera that's kind of a camera but is mostly an AI looking thing and then is mostly, but then has this dots in it that connects it to this other product?"
zh: 有很多，我一直看到我们设计新图标当我们本可以使用通用图标像，“噢，如果我们使用一个相机那是一种相机但主要是一个 AI 看起来的东西然后主要，但然后有点在它里面连接它到那个其他产品，那不是很酷吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're like, people just, it's a camera.
zh: 而你像，人们只是，它是一个相机。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just put the camera in.
zh: 只要把相机放进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you could add a little thing to it, and that's how you get people to use your products.
zh: 也许你可以加一个小东西给它，那是你让人们使用你产品的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you do those three things, I think you typically can do well.
zh: 如果你做这三件事，我认为你通常可以做得好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, sorry, the fourth one would be more of the coda is be humble.
zh: 然后，抱歉，第四个会是更多尾声是保持谦逊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Constantly and always question yourself.
zh: 持续并且总是质疑你自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: Listen to others, listen to users and be open to being wrong.
zh: 听其他人，听用户并对犯错持开放态度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love these.
zh: 我喜欢这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: On that third point, I feel like AI Mode as the name is such a good example of clarity.
zh: 关于第三点，我觉得 AI Mode 这个名字是清晰度的一个很好的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is this?
zh: 这是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is AI Mode.
zh: 这是 AI Mode。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talked about it internally.
zh: 我们内部讨论过这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at it in the tab, it's like everyone know, it's like you see it and you'll know what it is or we could call it something random, but then what is that?
zh: 如果你在标签页里看它，就像大家都知道，就像你看到它就会知道它是什么，或者我们可以给它随便起个名，但那又是什么呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And now you're working against yourself.
zh: 然后你在跟自己作对。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I were to reflect back these three pieces of basically this is the book you would write to help people build more successful products, it's understand the problem you're solving for people deeply.
zh: 如果我要反思这三点，基本上这就是你会写来帮助人们构建更成功产品的书，就是深刻理解你为人们解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the job they're hiring you to do?
zh: 他们雇佣你去做的工作是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I love the, it's lowercase jobs to be done.
zh: 我喜欢这个，这是小写的待办任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not like the rigorous whole thing that everyone-
zh: 不像大家通常说的那种严谨的整套东西——

speaker: Robby Stein
en: Exactly. Lowercase for sure.
zh: 没错。肯定是小写的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is just like why are people hiring your product to solve a problem for them?
zh: 这就像人们为什么要雇你的产品为他们解决问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: What problem are they solving?
zh: 他们在解决什么问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like basically figure out what problem they're having then very, through data, understand the problem and whether you are solving it.
zh: 所以就像基本上找出他们遇到了什么问题，然后通过数据，非常地，理解这个问题以及你是否在解决它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it's just keep it really simple.
zh: 然后就是让它保持非常简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Clarity over cleverness essentially.
zh: 本质上就是清晰胜过聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly, yes.
zh: 没错，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And be humble.
zh: 并且要谦逊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And be humble.
zh: 并且要谦逊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, important.
zh: 好的，这很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there an example that we haven't talked about that shows this in action of just, cool, here's the problem we found.
zh: 有没有我们没谈论过的例子展示了这一点，就是，酷，这是我们找到的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's how we figured out this is the solution and if we're succeeding, and then here's a very simple way of solving it?
zh: 这是我们弄清楚这是解决方案的方式，以及如果我们成功了，然后这里有一个非常简单的解决方法？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean honestly, this Close Friends example, I can give you more from Instagram days was really wild.
zh: 我的意思是老实说，这个 Close Friends 的例子，我可以给你更多 Instagram 时期的例子，真的很疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took two or three years to get Close Friends to work, and I think people, it totally failed originally.
zh: Close Friends 花了两三年才运作起来，我觉得人们，它最初完全失败了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the product that lets you add a private list of people and then you can post to your story and then only those people see it.
zh: 这个产品让你添加一个私人列表，然后你可以发布到你的快拍（Stories），然后只有那些人能看到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like this very exclusive private space so you can feel really comfortable sharing maybe more.
zh: 就像这个非常排他的私密空间，这样你可以感到非常舒适地分享，也许更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, green circle.
zh: 哦，绿色圆圈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Green circles, yes.
zh: 绿色圆圈，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one of the most popular, at least when I was there, was one of the most popular features of Stories and did really well, but it totally failed.
zh: 它是最受欢迎的功能之一，至少当我在那里的时候，是 Stories 最受欢迎的功能之一，而且做得真的很好，但它完全失败了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think what we found out was that you actually used a bunch of these techniques here.
zh: 我认为我们要发现的是你实际上在这里使用了一堆这些技术。
